messages:
alex: FYI I'm seeing a huge unexpected outbound transfer charge in the March billing -> ~24k on DataTransfer from S3. Looks tied to the checkpoints bucket. anyone else seeing this?

maria: whoa. can you paste the cost line item? cost center? :eyes:

alex: quick grab from cost explorer, filtered by product 'Amazon S3' and usage type: `DataTransfer-Out-Bytes`
```
UsageType,Region,Bytes,UnblendedCost
DataTransfer-Out-Bytes,eu-west-1->us-west-2,2345678901,23456.78
```

alex: path analysis shows most of the traffic from `s3://redwood-checkpoints-prod/models/` -> replicated-bucket in us-west-2. replicationRuleId `replica-prod-2025`.

sam: that replication rule was added last quarter for DR (cross-region replication). it should only include "latest" prefixes though. did the scope expand?

alex: looks like rule was updated by a script. the filter changed from prefix `live/` to nothing (whole-bucket) by accident during the migration on 2025-03-02. logs: `s3:PutBucketReplication` by terraform-batch-runner.

tina: also saw a big restore job on 2025-03-03 — model prefetcher restarted and re-downloaded checkpoints to new nodepool. could be double-counting transfer if replication and restore overlap.

maria: we need to confirm whether costs are cross-region storage replication charges or egress from restore to compute (EC2). both bill differently.

billing-bot: ALERT: high data-transfer detected. threshold exceeded for account `redwood-prod` on 2025-03-03 02:14Z. top source: s3://redwood-checkpoints-prod/models/ dest: us-west-2-replica (1.9TB).

alex: tl;dr root cause: accidental removal of replication prefix filter + an automated node rebalancer that pulled many older checkpoints into us-west-2 for prewarm. combined caused ~2TB cross-region transfer.

sam: immediate mitigation: 1) pause cross-region replication (set `Status: Disabled` for replication rule `replica-prod-2025`), 2) add missing prefix filter `Prefix: live/` back, 3) block restore job until we confirm only hot checkpoints are fetched.

alex: commands I ran:
```bash
# disable replication
aws s3api put-bucket-replication --bucket redwood-checkpoints-prod --replication-configuration '{"Role":"arn:aws:iam::123:role/s3-replication","Rules":[{"ID":"replica-prod-2025","Status":"Disabled","Prefix":""}]}'
# check inventory for bytes by prefix
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-checkpoints-prod --prefix models/ --query 'Contents[].{Key: Key, Size: Size}' --output json | jq -r '.[] | .Size' | awk '{s+= $1} END {print s}'
```

maria: can finance request a billing adjustment with AWS for accidental config change? file a support case, include timestamps and the `s3:PutBucketReplication` principal. we may get a partial credit.

tina: ops note: the nodeprewarm job uses label `prewarm=true`. we should change it to only fetch `models/live/` and set an environment var `CHECKPOINT_PREFETCH_WINDOW=7d` so only recent checkpoints are pulled. I'll make a patch.

sam: longer term suggestions: 1) tag replication rules with `owner` and `ticket`, 2) add terraform plan guardrail to reject replication without a filter, 3) add cost-alert rule for S3 replication bytes > 500GB/day.

alex: opened infra ticket INFRA-3122 with audit artifacts + timeline + suggested mitigations. assigning owners: @sam for replication fix, @tina for prefetch change, @maria to file billing case.

maria: filing case now, adding cost center and invoice refs. will confirm if AWS responds with credit.

tina: patched prewarm config in staging, will rollout to prod canary after 30m smoke.

billing-bot: NOTE: billing case # 789432 opened with AWS — status PENDING. added cost logs and `PutBucketReplication` CloudTrail entries.

alex: thanks team. will follow up with a short postmortem and preventive checklist. :white_check_mark:
